# MEMORANDUM

**To:** [Partner], Dilur Interactive, Inc. deal team
**From:** [Associate]
**Date:** November 11, 2026
**Re:** Dilur / Glesar Emberfall asset acquisition: issues to fix or negotiate before closing

**Privileged & Confidential | Attorney Work Product**

---

## Preliminary note on posture

The Asset Purchase Agreement (APA) was signed on **August 24, 2026**. Dilur is therefore already bound to it. The instruction refers to the period "before Dilur signs." I have read that to mean before Dilur signs anything further, chiefly:

- the IP Assignment Agreement, which is a Closing deliverable under APA §3.2(c) and §3.3(b);
- any amendment to the APA; and
- any special indemnity or escrow arrangement for the Composer Claim.

**Leverage point.** The APA calls the IP Assignment Agreement "the form attached as Exhibit A" (APA §1.1(n)). The APA copy in the folder shows Exhibit A only as "[Attached separately.]" We need to confirm whether the form in the folder was attached at signing.

- If it was attached, Dilur is arguably obliged to deliver it in that form at Closing. Any changes must then be negotiated as an amendment.
- If it was not attached, Dilur has more room to insist on changes.

**Governing law.** The APA (§11.8), the IP Assignment Agreement (§7.5) and the Key Employee Agreement (§12.5) are all governed by New York law.

**Key numbers:**

| Item | Amount / date | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Purchase Price | $48,500,000 | APA §2.5 |
| General Cap | 15% of the Purchase Price ($7,275,000) | APA §9.5(a) |
| Cap on Fundamental Representations | Purchase Price | APA §9.5(c) |
| Basket | $242,500 | APA §9.5(b) |
| Outside date | December 31, 2026 | APA §10.1(b) |

---

## Summary of issues, by priority

| # | Issue | Location | Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Schedule Update termination window has lapsed; deemed-cure risk on the Composer Claim | APA §6.7 (with Board Consent Recital C) | Closing / value |
| 2 | Dilur gives an uncapped indemnity to Glesar for all Assigned IP losses, including pre-Closing losses | IP Assignment Agreement §5.2 (with APA §11.12) | Value: unlimited exposure |
| 3 | The IP representation is pulled back under the $7,275,000 General Cap | IP Assignment Agreement §6.3 (with APA §§9.5(c), 11.12) | Value |
| 4 | Ms. Okoro's consent is needed to assign the Key Employee Agreement and the Wickline license; the APA does not require it | Key Employee Agreement §12.4; APA Schedule 4.4, §7.2(c) | Closing / value |
| 5 | The order-of-precedence clause is the root cause of Issues 2 and 3 | APA §11.12 | Value |
| 6 | Other consent and closing-condition gaps | APA Schedule 4.4, §§2.7, 7.2(d), 10.1(b) | Closing |
| 7 | Nightjar localization agreement | Nightjar Agreement | Does not bear on the deal |

---

## Issue 1: Dilur's 10-Business-Day window to terminate over the Schedule Update has lapsed

**Where:**
- APA §6.7 (Schedule Updates)
- APA §10.1(d)
- Dilur Board Consent, Recital C and Resolutions 2.1–2.3

**What the documents say:**

- Under APA §6.7, if a Schedule Update discloses a matter that would cause the §7.2(a) bring-down condition to fail, Buyer may terminate by notice "delivered within ten (10) Business Days after Buyer's receipt of that Schedule Update."
- If Buyer does not terminate, the update "shall be deemed to have cured any inaccuracy in or breach of any representation or warranty disclosed in it." This applies both for Article IX (indemnification) and for the Article VII closing conditions.
- The Board Consent (Recital C) records that Dilur received the September Schedule Update on **September 14, 2026**. The update discloses the composer's infringement and royalty claim (the "Composer Claim").

**Timing:**

- September 14, 2026 was a Monday.
- Counting ten Business Days under APA §1.1(d), the window closed on **Monday, September 28, 2026**. No New York bank holidays fall in that period.
- The Board Consent is dated **October 6, 2026**, eight days after the window closed. It directs an Objection Notice and a reservation of rights, but it does not, and could not, terminate the APA under §6.7.
- Today is November 11, 2026, so the termination right under §6.7 / §10.1(d) is gone.

**Why it matters to Dilur:**

1. **Deemed cure of the representations.** Glesar will argue that the update cured the inaccuracies in:
   - §4.7 (Litigation);
   - §4.9(c) (non-infringement, no pending claims); and
   - Schedule 4.9(d) ("None" for royalty obligations).

   If that argument succeeds:
   - Dilur loses its §9.2(a) indemnity claim for these breaches. This includes the Fundamental Representation treatment of §4.9, which is otherwise capped at the full Purchase Price.
   - Dilur cannot rely on §7.2(a) to refuse to close.

   The Board's "objection" does not stop the deemed cure. Section 6.7 turns only on whether Dilur terminated, not on whether it accepted the update.

2. **Dilur may be obliged to close over a known infringement claim against the soundtrack it is buying.** The fallback closing protections are uncertain:
   - §7.2(d) (no pending proceeding challenging Seller's ownership of the Assigned IP) may not apply, because an infringement and royalty claim does not necessarily challenge ownership.
   - §10.1(c) depends on a breach that has not been cured, and Glesar will say the update cured it.

3. **What survives.** The deemed cure applies to "any inaccuracy in or breach of any representation or warranty." It does not, on its face, reach:
   - the **Excluded Liabilities** allocation in §2.4(d) (pre-Closing infringement) and §2.4(e) (proceedings arising from pre-Closing facts); or
   - the indemnity for Excluded Liabilities in §9.2(c), which is outside the General Cap and the basket, because §9.5(a)–(b) apply only to §9.2(a).

   This is Dilur's strongest remaining protection. However, IP Assignment Agreement §5.2 would reverse it (see Issue 2). Fixing Issue 2 is therefore essential to protecting Dilur on the Composer Claim.

**Arguments that remain available (to preserve, not to rely on):**

- Section 6.7 covers only matters that "first arise[], or first come[] to the Knowledge of Seller, after the Signing Date." Ms. Okoro is a Knowledge party (APA §1.1(p)) and was responsible for audio direction (Key Employee Agreement §2.2).
- If Glesar knew of the composer dispute before August 24, 2026, the notice is arguably not a valid "Schedule Update" at all. In that case:
  - no deemed cure applies; and
  - the pre-signing non-disclosure may support a fraud claim, which escapes both the §9.5 limitations (§9.5(d)) and the exclusive-remedy clause (§9.6).

  We should investigate this promptly. The September Schedule Update itself and the composer's correspondence are not in the folder.
- We should also confirm the actual date and method of receipt under §11.2. The Board Consent recital is the only evidence in the folder, and we have assumed it is accurate. We should **not** advise the client that the window may still be open.

**Recommended actions:**

1. **Confirm the Objection Notice was sent.** Board Resolution 2.1 directs it, but it is not in the folder. It should be sent if it has not been. It should include the Resolution 2.4 reminder that, under APA §6.1, Glesar may not settle the Composer Claim without Dilur's consent.

2. **Negotiate an APA amendment** under the authority in Board Resolution 2.3. The amendment itself needs further Board approval, so a Board approval step should be built into the timetable. It should include:
   - a special, uncapped indemnity for the Composer Claim;
   - an escrow or holdback; and
   - an express override of the §6.7 deemed cure for the Composer Claim.

   Proposed language:

   > **Section 9.8 Composer Claim.** Notwithstanding Section 6.7, Section 9.5 or any other provision of this Agreement or any other Transaction Document, (a) the September Schedule Update shall not be deemed to have cured any inaccuracy in or breach of Sections 4.7 or 4.9 or Schedule 4.9(d) for any purpose; (b) all Liabilities arising out of or relating to the Composer Claim, whether arising before or after the Closing, are Excluded Liabilities; and (c) Seller shall indemnify the Buyer Indemnitees for all Losses arising out of or relating to the Composer Claim, without regard to the General Cap or the basket in Section 9.5(b). At the Closing, Buyer shall deposit $[●] of the Purchase Price with [Escrow Agent] (the "**Composer Escrow**") to secure Seller's obligations under this Section 9.8, to be released upon the final, non-appealable resolution of the Composer Claim and payment of all related Losses.

3. **Add a closing condition** on the Composer Claim:

   > **7.2(f)** Either (i) the Composer Claim shall have been settled or dismissed with prejudice on terms reasonably satisfactory to Buyer, with a full release of the Purchased Assets and Buyer, or (ii) Seller shall have obtained from the composer an assignment or license of all rights in the Emberfall Soundtrack necessary for Buyer's exploitation, in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to Buyer.

4. **Outside date.** The outside date is December 31, 2026 (§10.1(b)). Glesar may resist an amendment and run out the clock, or Dilur may need more time to resolve the Composer Claim. We should consider whether an extension of the outside date is in Dilur's interest.

---

## Issue 2: Dilur's uncapped indemnity of Glesar for all Assigned IP losses, including pre-Closing losses

**Where:**
- IP Assignment Agreement §5.2 (Indemnification by Assignee)
- APA §11.12 (Order of Precedence)
- Conflicts with APA §§2.3, 2.4(d), 2.4(e), 9.3 and 9.5

**What the documents say:**

IP Assignment Agreement §5.2 requires Dilur, as Assignee, to indemnify Glesar and its members, managers, officers, employees and agents against:

> all Losses arising out of or relating to the Assigned IP or the ownership, use, licensing, distribution or other exploitation of the Assigned IP, **whether arising before or after the Effective Date**.

It also provides that Dilur's obligations "**are not subject to any limitation in the Purchase Agreement**."

**Why it matters to Dilur:**

1. **It reverses the APA's risk allocation.**
   - APA §2.4(d) makes "all Liabilities arising from pre-Closing infringement by or use of the Assigned IP" Excluded Liabilities retained by Seller.
   - APA §2.3 limits Dilur's assumed liabilities to post-Closing liabilities.
   - Section 5.2 makes Dilur responsible for Glesar's own pre-Closing infringement.

2. **The IP Assignment Agreement controls on this point.**
   - Under APA §11.12, "the IP Assignment Agreement shall control on matters concerning Assigned IP."
   - Glesar will argue that indemnification for Assigned IP losses is such a matter, so that §5.2 overrides §2.4(d) and the indemnity for Excluded Liabilities in §9.2(c).
   - IP Assignment Agreement §6.1 says the agreement is "subject to the terms of" the APA. That helps Dilur, but it is an uncertain counterweight to a specific precedence clause and to §5.2's express statement that it is "not subject to any limitation."

3. **It is uncapped.**
   - The APA's General Cap of 15% of the Purchase Price ($7,275,000) limits Buyer only for claims under §9.3(a) (Buyer representations).
   - It never reaches a freestanding indemnity in another Transaction Document.
   - Section 5.2 also disclaims all APA limitations expressly.

   Dilur's exposure is therefore unlimited.

4. **It defeats Dilur's position on the Composer Claim.**
   - Board Resolution 2.2(b) relies on §2.4(d)/(e) to treat the Composer Claim as an Excluded Liability.
   - Under §5.2, Dilur would instead have to indemnify Glesar for it.
   - Read with the deemed-cure risk in Issue 1, this would move the whole Composer Claim onto Dilur, with no cap.

5. **It makes the Seller indemnity circular.** Any Buyer claim under IP Assignment Agreement §5.1 for an infringement breach could be met by a Glesar counterclaim under §5.2 for the same Losses.

**Recommended fix:** Narrow §5.2 to the market-standard Buyer indemnity, covering post-Closing exploitation by Dilur only, and align it with the APA.

> **5.2 Indemnification by Assignee.** From and after the Effective Date, Assignee shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless the Assignor Indemnitees from and against all Losses arising out of any third-party claim to the extent arising from Assignee's ownership, use, licensing, distribution or other exploitation of the Assigned IP **after the Effective Date**, **excluding** any Losses (a) that constitute Excluded Liabilities under the Purchase Agreement, including under Sections 2.4(d) and 2.4(e) thereof, (b) arising from any facts or circumstances existing on or before the Effective Date, including the Composer Claim, or (c) for which Assignor is obligated to indemnify any Assignee Indemnitee under Section 5.1 or Article IX of the Purchase Agreement. Assignee's obligations under this Section 5.2 are subject to the limitations in Section 9.5 of the Purchase Agreement, applied as if this Section 5.2 were Section 9.3(a) of the Purchase Agreement.

Alternatively, delete §5.2. Dilur's indemnity for Assumed Liabilities under APA §9.3(c) already covers the legitimate post-Closing risk. Either way, also fix APA §11.12 (see Issue 5).

---

## Issue 3: The IP Assignment Agreement pulls the IP representation back under the General Cap

**Where:**
- IP Assignment Agreement §6.3 (Liability for Intellectual Property Matters)
- Conflicts with APA §9.5(c) and §9.1
- Given controlling effect by APA §11.12

**What the documents say:**

- APA §9.5(c) designates §4.9 (Intellectual Property) as a **Fundamental Representation**, together with §4.1 and §4.2. Fundamental Representations are:
  - excluded from the General Cap and the basket; and
  - subject only to a cap equal to the Purchase Price of $48,500,000.
- IP Assignment Agreement §6.3 provides: "Assignor's liability for any inaccuracy in or breach of Section 4.9 of the Purchase Agreement or Section 3 of this Agreement **shall be subject to the General Cap**."
- APA §11.12 says the IP Assignment Agreement controls on matters concerning the Assigned IP.

**Why it matters to Dilur:**

- The Assigned IP is the asset Dilur is paying for: the Emberfall Game Code, Marks and Soundtrack, plus *Emberfall III* in development.
- Under §6.3, Dilur's recovery for title, ownership, sufficiency or infringement defects in that IP falls from up to $48,500,000 to **$7,275,000**. That is 15% of the Purchase Price.
- That $7,275,000 is also shared with every other general representation claim. The General Cap is aggregate.
- Section 6.3 picks up the IP Assignment Agreement's own §3 representations (title, non-infringement and the incorporated §4.9). This undermines IP Assignment Agreement §6.2, which grants those representations Fundamental Representation survival.
- The §5.1 Seller indemnity "in accordance with Article IX" may also be read to import the basket.

The result undercuts the APA's carve-out structure at the most important point. Under §11.12 the narrower provision would likely prevail.

**Recommended fix:**

1. **Delete IP Assignment Agreement §6.3** and replace it with:

   > **6.3 Liability for Intellectual Property Matters.** The representations and warranties in Section 3 of this Agreement, and those in Section 4.9 of the Purchase Agreement, are Fundamental Representations for all purposes of the Purchase Agreement. Assignor's liability for any inaccuracy in or breach of them is not subject to the General Cap or the basket in Section 9.5(b) of the Purchase Agreement and is limited only as provided in Section 9.5(c) of the Purchase Agreement.

2. **Conform §5.1:** "...in accordance with the procedures in Section 9.4 of the Purchase Agreement and subject only to the limitations applicable to Fundamental Representations under Section 9.5(c) thereof."

3. **Amend APA §11.12** so that the APA's indemnification terms prevail (see Issue 5).

---

## Issue 4: Ms. Okoro's prior written consent is needed to assign the Key Employee Agreement and the Wickline toolkit license, and the APA does not provide for it

**Where:**
- Key Employee Agreement §12.4 (Assignment), §7.2(b) and (e) (Wickline license), Recital C and Exhibit A
- APA Schedule 2.1(c), item 1 (Key Employee Agreement listed as an Assigned Contract)
- APA §6.4
- APA Schedule 4.4 ("None. No third-party consents are required.")
- APA §§3.2(d), 4.3(c), 4.4, 6.3 and 7.2(c)

**What the documents say:**

- Ms. Okoro personally owns the **Wickline** engine toolkit. It is a prior invention under §7.2(a) and is used to build Emberfall (Recital C).
- Glesar holds only a **non-exclusive** license under §7.2(b). That license is "irrevocable (except as provided in Section 12.4)" and transferable "only in accordance with Section 12.4" (§7.2(e)).
- Section 12.4 bars Glesar from assigning or transferring the agreement or any of its rights, "including the license granted in Section 7.2, **without the prior written consent of Employee**." This applies whether the transfer occurs by "**sale of all or substantially all** of the Company's assets, or otherwise."
- Any non-compliant transfer is **void**, and "the license granted in Section 7.2 **terminates**."
- The APA lists the Key Employee Agreement as an Assigned Contract, and Dilur must assume it at Closing (§6.4).
- Schedule 4.4 states that no consents are required.
- The consent closing condition in §7.2(c) covers only consents "listed on Schedule 4.4." Okoro's consent is therefore **not a closing condition**.

**Note on the trigger.** Section 12.4's "or otherwise" language almost certainly captures this sale. It is also arguable that the Emberfall sale is itself a sale of all or substantially all of Glesar's assets. Glesar's other titles are Excluded Assets under Schedule 2.2, so we should check the relative size of the Emberfall assets.

**Why it matters to Dilur:**

1. **Dilur could have to close without the Wickline license.**
   - Under APA §2.7, an unconsented contract is simply not assigned, and Glesar provides the "benefits" through a pass-through arrangement.
   - That workaround is itself likely a prohibited "transfer... of any of its rights" under §12.4.
   - Worse, a purported assignment at Closing would terminate the license outright.
   - Glesar's §9.4 obligation to provide a pass-through arrangement may then be impossible to perform.

2. **The Emberfall Game Code and *Emberfall III* may depend on Wickline.**
   - Wickline covers the level editor, shaders, animation runtime and build tools (Exhibit A).
   - Without the license, Dilur's ability to ship, patch, port and develop the franchise is at risk. The ownership of Company Modifications under §7.2(d) is "subject to Employee's underlying rights."
   - This goes directly to the value of the Purchased Assets.

3. **Ms. Okoro holds leverage.** She is the Creative Director Dilur is acquiring and a Knowledge party. She can refuse consent or price it.

4. **Representations and remedies.**
   - The disclosures in Schedule 4.4 / §4.4, §4.3(c) and §4.9(b) (sufficiency of IP) are inaccurate.
   - Indemnity after Closing is a poor substitute for the license itself.
   - Any §4.9 claim also runs into Issue 3 (General Cap) and possibly the deemed-cure mechanism in Issue 1 if Glesar discloses this by Schedule Update.

**Recommended fix:**

1. **Require Ms. Okoro's written consent as a Closing condition and correct Schedule 4.4.** Proposed amendment:

   > **Schedule 4.4 – Consents.** 1. Written consent of Tamsin Okoro, under Section 12.4 of the Key Employee Agreement, to the assignment to Buyer of the Key Employee Agreement and of the license of the Wickline Toolkit granted in Section 7.2 thereof.
   >
   > **7.2(g)** Buyer shall have received (i) the consent described in item 1 of Schedule 4.4, and (ii) a written confirmation from Tamsin Okoro that the license in Section 7.2 of the Key Employee Agreement, as assigned to Buyer, is in full force and effect, has not terminated, and extends to Buyer and its Affiliates and successors, in each case in form and substance satisfactory to Buyer in its sole discretion.

2. **Better still, obtain a direct license from Ms. Okoro to Dilur** at Closing. It should be perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free, freely assignable and sublicensable to Dilur's Affiliates and successors, and should not be terminable on any future transfer. Ideally, Dilur should also obtain a source-code deposit of commit `wl-7c41e9a` and later versions. Proposed consent language:

   > Employee hereby consents to the assignment to Dilur Interactive, Inc. of the Agreement, including the license in Section 7.2, and agrees that (a) such assignment shall not cause the license to terminate, and (b) Section 12.4 shall not apply to any future assignment by Dilur to an Affiliate or to any acquirer of the Emberfall franchise.

3. **Pursue a new Dilur employment agreement** for Ms. Okoro, signed at or before Closing. Assignment of the existing agreement also carries the §5.5 Good Reason / severance exposure, for example if her title or creative responsibilities are diminished within Dilur.

4. **Make the §2.7 fallback inapplicable** to the Key Employee Agreement. Add a special indemnity covering any loss of Wickline rights, outside the General Cap.

---

## Issue 5: APA §11.12, the order-of-precedence clause, is the root cause of Issues 2 and 3

**Where:** APA §11.12.

**What it says:** "[T]he IP Assignment Agreement shall control on matters concerning Assigned IP, and otherwise this Agreement shall control."

**Why it matters to Dilur:**

- Nearly every indemnity and liability question in this deal "concerns Assigned IP."
- The clause lets a closing-date conveyancing document override the negotiated risk allocation in the APA's Articles II and IX.
- Fixing §5.2 and §6.3 alone leaves Dilur exposed to any other conflicting provision in the IP Assignment Agreement or the short-form assignments.

**Recommended fix (APA amendment):**

> **11.12 Order of Precedence.** In the event of any conflict or inconsistency between this Agreement and any other Transaction Document, this Agreement shall control, except that the IP Assignment Agreement shall control solely with respect to the mechanics of conveyance and recordation of the Assigned IP. Without limiting the foregoing, nothing in any other Transaction Document shall expand the Assumed Liabilities, limit the Excluded Liabilities, impose any indemnification obligation on Buyer, or limit any right or remedy of the Buyer Indemnitees under Article IX.

Also add to IP Assignment Agreement §6.1: "In the event of any conflict between this Agreement and the Purchase Agreement regarding indemnification, liability or the allocation of Liabilities, the Purchase Agreement controls."

---

## Issue 6: Other consent and closing-condition gaps (secondary)

1. **Schedule 4.4 / platform and middleware contracts.**
   - Schedule 2.1(c), items 2–3, lists platform distribution and middleware license agreements as Assigned Contracts "as listed in the data room index."
   - These commonly require counterparty consent. Schedule 4.4 nonetheless lists none.
   - We should review those contracts and add any required consents to Schedule 4.4 and the §7.2(c) condition.

2. **APA §7.2(d).** This condition is limited to proceedings challenging the transaction or "Seller's ownership" of the Assigned IP. It should be broadened:

   > (d) no action, suit, claim or proceeding shall be pending or threatened that challenges the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, Seller's ownership of, or the right to exploit, any Assigned IP, or that alleges that any Assigned IP infringes the Intellectual Property of any Person.

3. **APA §6.7 going forward.** Future Schedule Updates carry the same deemed-cure risk. Proposed fix:
   - delete the deemed cure; or
   - limit it to the closing conditions only, preserving Article IX rights; and
   - exclude Fundamental Representations from it.

   In any event, calendar any future Schedule Update immediately on receipt.

4. **Outside date.** December 31, 2026 (§10.1(b)) is seven weeks away. We should coordinate the amendment timetable, including the further Board approval required under Board Resolution 2.3.

---

## Issue 7: Nightjar Localization Services Agreement

**Where:** nightjar_localization_services_agreement.md (Dilur–Nightjar Localization Ltd., dated February 2, 2026).

**Conclusion:** This agreement **does not bear on the transaction**. It is an unrelated, pre-existing Dilur vendor contract:

- Glesar is not a party.
- It is not an Assigned Contract, Purchased Asset or Transaction Document.
- It is not referenced in the APA, the IP Assignment Agreement or the Board Consent.
- Its assignment clause (§11.4) restricts Dilur's and Nightjar's assignment of that agreement. The Emberfall acquisition does not trigger it.

**One practical note, not a deal issue.** If Dilur later uses Nightjar to localize Emberfall titles after Closing, it should do so under a new Statement of Work. In that case, check that:
- the Emberfall materials provided are properly licensed "Dilur Materials"; and
- Dilur's indemnity of Nightjar under §8.2 (uncapped by §9.3(a)) does not pick up Composer Claim or Wickline exposure.

This is another reason to resolve Issues 1 and 4 before Closing.

---

## Missing documents and information

We need the following, which are not in the folder:

1. **The Disclosure Schedule** delivered at signing, and the **September Schedule Update** itself. We need these to confirm:
   - the receipt date and method (APA §11.2);
   - exactly what was disclosed; and
   - whether the Composer Claim truly "first arose" after signing.
2. **The Objection Notice** directed by Board Resolution 2.1, with proof of delivery. We need to confirm that it was sent and when.
3. **Composer Claim materials:** the claim or complaint, any composer agreement or work-for-hire/assignment with Glesar, and any royalty arrangements. These bear on APA §4.9(d) and Schedule 4.9(d).
4. **The executed Exhibit A**, the form of IP Assignment Agreement attached at signing, if any. We need to confirm whether the folder version is the agreed form (see the preliminary note).
5. **The data room index and the platform distribution and middleware license agreements** (Schedule 2.1(c), items 2–3), to identify required consents.
6. **Forms of the Bill of Sale and the Assignment and Assumption Agreement.** These are also Transaction Documents and could contain provisions that conflict with the APA.
7. **Wickline materials:** confirmation of the toolkit's role in the Emberfall Game Code and *Emberfall III*, and the deposited commit `wl-7c41e9a`.
8. **Employee and contractor IP assignments** supporting APA §4.9(d), and any open-source review supporting Schedule 4.9(e).
9. **The prior Board approval** referred to in Board Consent Recital B, and the management report and outside counsel advice referred to in Recital E.
10. **Any term sheet or correspondence** with Ms. Okoro about her post-Closing employment with Dilur.

---

## Recommended next steps

1. **Immediately:**
   - Confirm the Objection Notice was delivered; if not, send it.
   - Investigate when Glesar first knew of the Composer Claim.
   - Calendar the December 31, 2026 outside date.
2. **Propose to Glesar a single APA amendment** covering:
   - the Composer Claim special indemnity, escrow and deemed-cure override (Issue 1);
   - revised §11.12 (Issue 5);
   - corrected Schedule 4.4, the Okoro consent and Wickline confirmation as closing conditions, and a broadened §7.2(d) (Issues 4 and 6); and
   - an agreed revised form of IP Assignment Agreement that deletes or narrows §5.2 (Issue 2) and replaces §6.3 (Issue 3).
3. **Obtain Board approval** of the amendment under Board Resolution 2.3.
4. **Approach Ms. Okoro**, coordinated with Glesar under APA §6.3, for her consent and a direct Wickline license.
5. **Dilur should not sign the IP Assignment Agreement in its current form.**

# MEMORANDUM

**To:** Dilur Interactive, Inc. Deal Team
**From:** Outside Counsel
**Date:** November 11, 2026
**Re:** Emberfall Asset Acquisition from Glesar Studios LLC: Issues Requiring Correction or Negotiation

---

## I. Summary

We reviewed the following documents:

- the Asset Purchase Agreement dated August 24, 2026 (the "**APA**");
- Dilur's board consent dated October 6, 2026 (the "**Board Consent**");
- the form of Intellectual Property Assignment Agreement to be delivered at Closing (the "**IPAA**");
- the Key Employee Agreement between Glesar and Tamsin Okoro (the "**KEA**"); and
- the Nightjar Localization and Quality Assurance Services Agreement.

The APA is already signed. Any change to it therefore requires a written amendment signed by both parties under APA Section 11.3. The IPAA is still a form exhibit, so it can be revised before Closing.

The most serious problems sit in the IPAA. Under APA **Section 11.12 (Order of Precedence)**, "the IP Assignment Agreement shall control on matters concerning Assigned IP, and otherwise this Agreement shall control." Because of this clause, unfavorable terms in the IPAA override the APA's protections for Dilur on the core asset Dilur is buying.

We found three issues, listed in priority order:

1. **IPAA Section 5.2.** Dilur gives Glesar an uncapped indemnity for all Assigned IP losses, including pre-Closing losses.
2. **IPAA Section 6.3.** Glesar's liability for the IP representation is pulled back under the $7,275,000 General Cap.
3. **KEA Section 12.4.** Ms. Okoro's consent is required to assign her Wickline toolkit license, but the APA neither lists that consent nor makes it a closing condition.

The Nightjar agreement does not bear on the deal (Part IV). Missing documents and information are listed in Part V.

---

## II. Key Deal Terms Referenced

| Term | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Purchase Price | $48,500,000 | APA Section 2.5 |
| General Cap | 15% of the Purchase Price ($7,275,000) | APA Section 9.5(a) |
| Fundamental Representations | Sections 4.1, 4.2 and 4.9 (IP), excluded from the General Cap and the basket, and capped at the Purchase Price | APA Section 9.5(c) |
| Pre-Closing IP liabilities | Excluded Liabilities retained by Seller | APA Section 2.4(d) |
| Order of precedence | IPAA controls on Assigned IP matters; otherwise the APA controls | APA Section 11.12 |
| Governing law | New York | APA Section 11.8; IPAA Section 7.5; KEA Section 12.5 |

## III. Issues

### Issue 1: Uncapped Buyer Indemnity of Seller for All Assigned IP Losses, Including Pre-Closing Losses

**Document:** IPAA, Section 5.2 (read with APA Sections 2.4(d), 9.3, 9.5 and 11.12)

**What it says.** IPAA Section 5.2 requires Dilur, as Assignee, to "indemnify, defend and hold harmless the Assignor Indemnitees from and against all Losses arising out of or relating to the Assigned IP or the ownership, use, licensing, distribution or other exploitation of the Assigned IP, *whether arising before or after the Effective Date*." It adds that Dilur's obligations "*are not subject to any limitation in the Purchase Agreement*."

**Why it matters to Dilur.**

- **It reverses the APA's allocation of risk.** APA Section 2.4(d) makes "all Liabilities arising from pre-Closing infringement by or use of the Assigned IP" Excluded Liabilities retained by Glesar. APA Section 9.2(c) requires Glesar to indemnify Dilur for them. IPAA Section 5.2 does the opposite: Dilur would indemnify Glesar and its members for the same pre-Closing losses.
- **The IPAA prevails.** Section 5.2 plainly concerns Assigned IP, so APA Section 11.12 gives it controlling effect over Section 2.4(d). Glesar could argue that the two obligations cancel out. At best that leads to circular claims; at worst Dilur's protection disappears.
- **No cap applies.** The APA General Cap in Section 9.5(a) covers only claims under Sections 9.2(a) and 9.3(a), which are rep-and-warranty claims. This freestanding IPAA indemnity falls outside the cap, and it also expressly disclaims every APA limitation. Dilur's exposure is unlimited, and it covers Glesar's members as well as Glesar.
- **There is a known live exposure.** The Board Consent (Recital C) records a pending claim by the Emberfall Soundtrack composer alleging pre-Closing infringement and unpaid royalties. As drafted, Section 5.2 would make Dilur responsible for indemnifying Glesar against that claim. The Board Consent (Resolution 2.2(b)) takes the position that this liability belongs to Glesar.
- **There is no reciprocity.** Glesar's indemnity in IPAA Section 5.1 runs "in accordance with Article IX of the Purchase Agreement," which means it remains subject to the APA's caps and baskets. Dilur's indemnity is uncapped.

**Recommended fix.**

1. Limit Dilur's indemnity to losses from Dilur's own post-Closing exploitation, mirroring APA Section 2.3(b).
2. Expressly carve out Excluded Liabilities.
3. Make the indemnity subject to APA Article IX.
4. Separately, amend APA Section 11.12 so that the IPAA cannot override Articles II or IX (see Issue 2).

**Proposed replacement language for IPAA Section 5.2:**

> **5.2 Indemnification by Assignee.** From and after the Effective Date, Assignee shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless the Assignor Indemnitees from and against all Losses to the extent arising out of the ownership, use, licensing, distribution or other exploitation of the Assigned IP by or on behalf of Assignee *after* the Effective Date; *provided* that Assignee shall have no obligation under this Section 5.2 with respect to (a) any Excluded Liability, including any Liability described in Section 2.4(d) or 2.4(e) of the Purchase Agreement, (b) any matter for which Assignor is obligated to indemnify any Assignee Indemnitee under Section 5.1 of this Agreement or Article IX of the Purchase Agreement, or (c) any claim asserted by any Person (including the composer of the Emberfall Soundtrack) to the extent arising from facts or circumstances existing on or before the Effective Date. Assignee's obligations under this Section 5.2 are subject to the procedures and limitations of Article IX of the Purchase Agreement as if this Section 5.2 were Section 9.3(c) of the Purchase Agreement.

### Issue 2: IP Representation Pulled Back Under the General Cap

**Document:** IPAA, Section 6.3 (read with APA Sections 9.5(a), 9.5(c) and 11.12)

**What it says.** IPAA Section 6.3 provides that "Assignor's liability for any inaccuracy in or breach of Section 4.9 of the Purchase Agreement or Section 3 of this Agreement *shall be subject to the General Cap*."

**Why it matters to Dilur.**

- Under APA Section 9.5(c), the Section 4.9 Intellectual Property representation is a **Fundamental Representation**. It is excluded from both the General Cap and the $242,500 basket, and it is capped only at the full Purchase Price of $48,500,000. That treatment was a central protection for Dilur, because the Emberfall IP (code, marks and soundtrack) is essentially the whole deal.
- IPAA Section 6.3 reverses that treatment. Because it concerns Assigned IP, APA Section 11.12 lets it control. As a result, Glesar's liability for title or infringement defects in the core IP would be capped at **15% of the Purchase Price ($7,275,000)** instead of $48,500,000.
- The cap also reaches the IPAA's own Section 3 representations on title and non-infringement, and the Section 4.9 representations that Section 3.4 incorporates by reference. Every route to an IP recovery is therefore capped.
- The provision also conflicts with IPAA Section 6.2. That section gives the Section 3 representations the longer survival period applicable to Fundamental Representations, which shows the parties intended Fundamental treatment.
- The pending Composer Claim (Board Consent, Recital C) implicates Section 4.9(c) and Schedule 4.9(d). A capped IP representation could leave Dilur materially under-protected on that claim alone.

**Recommended fix.**

1. **Delete IPAA Section 6.3 in its entirety.** Replace it with an express statement that the Section 3 representations are Fundamental Representations.
2. **Amend APA Section 11.12** so that the APA's allocation and indemnification provisions always prevail. Without this change, any future IPAA drafting slip will again override the APA.

**Proposed replacement for IPAA Section 6.3:**

> **6.3 Liability for Intellectual Property Matters.** The representations and warranties in Section 3 of this Agreement, and the representations and warranties in Section 4.9 of the Purchase Agreement as incorporated by Section 3.4, constitute Fundamental Representations for all purposes of the Purchase Agreement. Assignor's liability for any inaccuracy in or breach of them shall be subject only to the limitations applicable to Fundamental Representations under Section 9.5(c) of the Purchase Agreement, and shall not be subject to the General Cap or the basket in Section 9.5(b) of the Purchase Agreement.

**Proposed amendment to APA Section 11.12:**

> **11.12 Order of Precedence.** In the event of any conflict or inconsistency between this Agreement and any other Transaction Document, this Agreement shall control; *provided* that the IP Assignment Agreement shall control solely with respect to the mechanics of conveyance, recordation and further assurances concerning the Assigned IP. Notwithstanding the foregoing, no provision of any other Transaction Document shall expand the Assumed Liabilities, reduce the Excluded Liabilities, or modify Article IX (including Section 9.5) of this Agreement, unless that provision expressly references this Section 11.12 and is signed by both Parties.

### Issue 3: Ms. Okoro's Consent Is Required to Assign the Key Employee Agreement and the Wickline Toolkit License, and the APA Does Not Provide for It

**Document:** KEA, Section 12.4 (with KEA Sections 7.2(b) and 7.2(e); APA Schedule 2.1(c), Schedule 4.4, Sections 2.7, 4.4, 6.3, 6.4 and 7.2(c))

**What it says.**

- KEA Section 12.4 prohibits Glesar from assigning or transferring the KEA, "including the license granted in Section 7.2, *without the prior written consent of Employee*." The restriction applies expressly to a transfer by "*sale of all or substantially all* of the Company's assets, or otherwise."
- Any purported assignment in violation is "void," and on any such purported assignment "the license granted in Section 7.2 terminates."
- KEA Section 7.2(e) confirms that the Wickline license may be transferred "only in accordance with Section 12.4."

**Why it matters to Dilur.**

- **Wickline is embedded in Emberfall.** Under KEA Section 7.2(a), Ms. Okoro personally owns the Wickline engine toolkit (level and encounter editor, shader library, animation runtime, and build and asset-cooking utilities). Glesar holds only a non-exclusive license, and Recital C of the KEA says that license is used to develop Emberfall. The Emberfall Game Code, including *Emberfall III*, which is still in development, very likely depends on it. Without the license, Dilur may be unable to build, patch, port or ship the titles.
- **The asset sale triggers the consent right.** APA Schedule 2.1(c) lists the KEA as an Assigned Contract, and APA Section 6.4 requires its assignment at Closing. That transfer falls squarely within Section 12.4. If Glesar assigns without consent, the assignment is void and the license terminates. Dilur would then have no Wickline rights at all, and Glesar would lose them too.
- **The APA does not account for this.** APA Schedule 4.4 states: "None. No third-party consents are required." That statement is inaccurate and breaches APA Sections 4.3(c) and 4.4. The problems that follow are:
  - Glesar's efforts covenant in Section 6.3 covers only consents listed on Schedule 4.4.
  - The closing condition in Section 7.2(c) likewise covers only Schedule 4.4 consents.
  - The Seller deliverable in Section 3.2(d) is similarly limited.
  
  As a result, Dilur has no express closing condition protecting it and could be obligated to close and pay $48,500,000 without assured toolkit rights.
- **Section 2.7 does not solve the problem.** The workaround for non-assignable assets in APA Section 2.7 (a pass-through of benefits) does not help. Any purported transfer, including a back-to-back arrangement, risks triggering the termination of the license under KEA Section 12.4. The license is also limited to the Company's use, with sublicensing permitted only to contractors and distributors under Section 7.2(c).
- **The rep gap creates a secondary issue.** Glesar's Section 4.9(b) representation states that the Assigned IP and the licensed rights constitute all IP necessary to exploit Emberfall. That representation would be breached. However, a post-Closing indemnity claim is a poor substitute for actually holding the license. The claim would also depend on the outcome of Issue 2.
- **Ms. Okoro is also a Knowledge party.** Ms. Okoro is one of the three individuals whose knowledge counts as "Knowledge of Seller" under APA Section 1.1(p). Her consent negotiation should be handled carefully, because she has leverage both as licensor and as key employee.

**Recommended fix.**

1. **Amend APA Schedule 4.4** to list Ms. Okoro's written consent under KEA Section 12.4. This automatically brings the consent within APA Sections 3.2(d), 6.3 and 7.2(c).
2. **Add a specific closing condition and deliverable** so the point does not depend on the schedule alone. Preferably, require a direct license from Ms. Okoro to Dilur that is broader than the existing license. It should cover Dilur and its Affiliates and successors, allow freer sublicensing, and confirm that the Company Modifications under KEA Section 7.2(d) pass to Dilur.
3. **Reserve indemnity rights** for the inaccuracy in Schedule 4.4, and confirm that the KEA consent is not an Assumed Liability issue.

**Proposed new APA Section 7.2(f):**

> (f) Seller shall have delivered to Buyer (i) the written consent of Tamsin Okoro, in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to Buyer, under Section 12.4 of the Key Employee Agreement to the assignment of the Key Employee Agreement, including the license granted in Section 7.2 thereof, to Buyer, and confirming that such assignment will not cause the termination of that license; and (ii) a direct, non-exclusive, worldwide, perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free, fully paid-up license from Tamsin Okoro to Buyer and its Affiliates, successors and assigns of the Wickline Toolkit (as defined in the Key Employee Agreement) for the development, publication, distribution, operation and exploitation of the Emberfall franchise and any sequels, expansions, ports or remasters thereof, freely sublicensable in connection therewith and assignable to any acquirer of the Emberfall franchise, which license shall survive any termination of Ms. Okoro's employment or of the Key Employee Agreement.

**Proposed corrected Schedule 4.4:**

> **Schedule 4.4 – Consents**
> 1. Written consent of Tamsin Okoro under Section 12.4 of the Key Employee Agreement to the assignment to Buyer of the Key Employee Agreement and the Wickline Toolkit license granted in Section 7.2 thereof.
> 2. [Any consents required under the platform distribution and middleware license agreements listed on Schedule 2.1(c), to be confirmed upon review.]

## IV. The Nightjar Localization Services Agreement Does Not Bear on the Deal

The Nightjar Localization and Quality Assurance Services Agreement, dated February 2, 2026, is between Dilur and Nightjar Localization Ltd. It is unrelated to the Emberfall transaction:

- Glesar is not a party to it.
- It is not an Assigned Contract on APA Schedule 2.1(c).
- It does not reference Emberfall or the Purchased Assets.
- It predates the APA.

It is Dilur's own vendor contract and will continue unaffected by Closing. Nothing in it restricts the acquisition. Its assignment clause (Section 11.4) is relevant only if Dilur itself assigns that agreement.

There is one practical point. If Dilur later engages Nightjar to localize Emberfall titles, Emberfall builds would become "Dilur Materials," and Dilur would indemnify Nightjar for infringement by them under Nightjar Section 8.2. That makes it more important that Dilur not carry pre-Closing IP risk (Issues 1 and 2) and that it hold clean Wickline rights (Issue 3). This is a downstream commercial consideration, not a deal issue, and no changes to the Nightjar agreement are needed.
